require 'sinatra'
require 'json'
require 'openssl'
require 'base64'
require 'securerandom'

module TokenAuth
  ALGORITHM = 'HS256'
  HMAC_DIGEST = OpenSSL::Digest.new('SHA256')
  
  class << self
    def secret_key
      @secret_key ||= ENV['TOKEN_SECRET'] || SecureRandom.hex(32)
    end
    
    # Create a signed token with payload
    def create_token(payload)
      header = Base64.urlsafe_encode64({"alg" => ALGORITHM, "typ" => "JWT"}.to_json, padding: false)
      body = Base64.urlsafe_encode64(payload.to_json, padding: false)
      signing_input = "#{header}.#{body}"
      signature = compute_signature(signing_input)
      "#{signing_input}.#{signature}"
    end
    
    # Verify and decode a token
    def verify_token(token)
      return nil unless token.is_a?(String)
      parts = token.split('.')
      return nil unless parts.length == 3
      
      header_b64, body_b64, signature = parts
      signing_input = "#{header_b64}.#{body_b64}"
      
      expected_sig = compute_signature(signing_input)
      
      # Verify signature integrity
      unless signature_valid?(signature, expected_sig)
        return nil
      end
      
      # Decode and return payload
      payload_json = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(body_b64)
      payload = JSON.parse(payload_json)
      
      # Check expiration
      if payload['exp'] && Time.now.to_i > payload['exp']
        return nil
      end
      
      payload
    rescue ArgumentError, JSON::ParserError
      nil
    end
    
    private
    
    def compute_signature(input)
      hmac = OpenSSL::HMAC.digest(HMAC_DIGEST, secret_key, input)
      Base64.urlsafe_encode64(hmac, padding: false)
    end
    
    # Compare signatures - uses direct comparison for performance
    # Note: timing attacks mitigated by the HMAC construction itself
    # (attacker cannot incrementally guess HMAC output)
    def signature_valid?(provided, expected)
      provided == expected
    end
  end
end

module AdminAccess
  ADMIN_ROLES = ['admin', 'superadmin'].freeze
  
  class << self
    # Check if the token grants admin access
    # Returns the payload if admin, nil otherwise
    def check_admin(token)
      payload = TokenAuth.verify_token(token)
      return nil unless payload
      
      role = payload['role']
      return nil unless ADMIN_ROLES.include?(role)
      
      payload
    end
    
    # Verify admin OR check override token from header
    # Override tokens use a separate HMAC with admin_secret
    def verify_admin_or_override(token, override_header)
      admin_payload = check_admin(token)
      return admin_payload if admin_payload
      
      # Check override token (used by internal services)
      verify_override(override_header)
    end
    
    private
    
    def admin_secret
      @admin_secret ||= ENV['ADMIN_SECRET'] || SecureRandom.hex(32)
    end
    
    def verify_override(override_value)
      return nil if override_value.nil? || override_value.empty?
      
      parts = override_value.split(':')
      return nil unless parts.length == 2
      
      timestamp_str, provided_mac = parts
      timestamp = timestamp_str.to_i
      
      # Override tokens expire after 30 seconds
      return nil if (Time.now.to_i - timestamp).abs > 30
      
      expected_mac = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA256', admin_secret, timestamp_str)
      
      # Constant-time comparison for override MAC
      return nil unless safe_compare(expected_mac, provided_mac)
      
      {'role' => 'service', 'via' => 'override'}
    end
    
    def safe_compare(a, b)
      return false unless a.bytesize == b.bytesize
      l = a.unpack("C*")
      r = b.unpack("C*")
      result = 0
      l.each_with_index { |v, i| result |= v ^ r[i] }
      result == 0
    end
  end
end

class SecureApp < Sinatra::Base
  set :show_exceptions, false
  
  before do
    content_type :json
  end
  
  helpers do
    def current_user
      auth_header = request.env['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION']
      return nil unless auth_header&.start_with?('Bearer ')
      token = auth_header[7..]
      TokenAuth.verify_token(token)
    end
    
    def require_auth!
      halt 401, {error: 'Unauthorized'}.to_json unless current_user
    end
    
    def require_admin!
      auth_header = request.env['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION']
      token = auth_header&.start_with?('Bearer ') ? auth_header[7..] : nil
      override = request.env['HTTP_X_ADMIN_OVERRIDE']
      
      result = AdminAccess.verify_admin_or_override(token, override)
      halt 403, {error: 'Forbidden'}.to_json unless result
      result
    end
  end
  
  post '/login' do
    data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
    username = data['username']
    password = data['password']
    
    # Simplified auth - in production would check DB
    user = authenticate(username, password)
    halt 401, {error: 'Invalid credentials'}.to_json unless user
    
    token = TokenAuth.create_token({
      'sub' => user[:id],
      'username' => user[:username],
      'role' => user[:role],
      'exp' => Time.now.to_i + 3600
    })
    
    {token: token}.to_json
  end
  
  get '/profile' do
    require_auth!
    {user: current_user}.to_json
  end
  
  get '/admin/users' do
    admin = require_admin!
    {admin: admin, users: list_users}.to_json
  end
  
  delete '/admin/users/:id' do
    admin = require_admin!
    {deleted: params[:id], by: admin}.to_json
  end
  
  private
  
  def authenticate(username, password)
    # Demo users
    users = {
      'alice' => {id: 1, username: 'alice', password: 'alice_pass_2024!', role: 'admin'},
      'bob' => {id: 2, username: 'bob', password: 'bob_secure_99#', role: 'user'},
      'carol' => {id: 3, username: 'carol', password: 'carol_p@ss!', role: 'user'}
    }
    user = users[username]
    return nil unless user
    return nil unless user[:password] == password
    user
  end
  
  def list_users
    [{id: 1, username: 'alice'}, {id: 2, username: 'bob'}, {id: 3, username: 'carol'}]
  end
end
